title: In a locally connected space the open subsets are locally connected and the connected components are open

standard_prerequisites.name: The definition of local connectedness through a fundamental system of connected neighbourhoods, and the notion of a connected component
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Set up in the author's section on connected components, immediately before the counted statement
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the hypothesis and the two conclusions of the statement.

core_obligations: Part (1): for an open subset U and a point of U the proof restricts the fundamental system of connected neighbourhoods to those contained in U, which is again a fundamental system of connected neighbourhoods, so U is locally connected (proof lines 1049-1058).
Part (2): the proof shows that the connected component of a point is a neighbourhood of that point, by exhibiting a connected neighbourhood contained in the component (proof lines 1058-1061).

Conclusion: a set that is a neighbourhood of each of its points is open, so the components are open, and hence so are the components of open subsets, which also gives the fundamental-system statement of the last sentence (proof lines 1061-1062).
proof_roadmap: (1) 把 x 的连通邻域基本系限制到开集 U 内，仍是 U 中连通邻域的基本系。
(2) 说明每个点的连通分量包含一个连通邻域，从而是该点的邻域；「是每一点的邻域」即开，故连通分量开；开子集的分量同理开。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the behaviour of local connectedness and of connected components in a locally connected space (author lemma at source lines 1036-1046, label lemma-locally-connected): opens are locally connected, components are open, and every point has a fundamental system of open connected neighbourhoods. The proof (source lines 1048-1063) works with the fundamental system of connected neighbourhoods of a point: restricting it to an open subset gives (1), and exhibiting a connected neighbourhood inside the component shows the component is a neighbourhood of each of its points, hence open (proof lines 1058-1061). The statement is the local counterpart of the connectedness lemma earlier in the section. H2.
